lectures.title: L1 Analyzing the Current Business Scenario

cards.title: Why innovation: the set-up
lines: Course aim: commercialise innovations and business models for growth, jobs, national development.

New models earn in ways users do not see (lecturer's recording-era examples: **Ola/Uber** taxi firms with no taxis, **Alibaba** retail with no inventory, free **WhatsApp/YouTube/Gmail/Facebook** that still profit).

cards.title: Business environment
lines: **Internal**: a firm has some control.
**External**: very little control. Example: **politics** (parties, policies, regulation keep changing).

cards.title: Pressures on business
lines: Slide lists **4**: reducing PLCs, increasing expectations, high uncertainty, global impact.
Lecture adds a 5th, **increasing heterogeneity**. If asked for the slide list, use 4.

items.label: Increasing expectations
items.detail: Low cost + high quality + fast delivery together

items.label: Global impact
items.detail: Local events travel (Apple: US, made in China, sold worldwide)

cards.title: Product life cycle (PLC)
lines: Four phases: **introduction, growth, maturity, decline**.
Consumer durables: **10-20 years** before, **2-3 years** in the lecture's comparison. Less time for new product development.
Examples: B&W TV 20-30 years, then colour, flat screen, HD, plasma, LED, LCD. Mobiles in India since **1996**, described in the lecture as ~2-year life.

cards.title: Expectations and heterogeneity
lines: Customers now want **low cost, high quality, fast delivery simultaneously**: no trade-off (they compare Amazon, Flipkart, eBay, Jabong).
**Heterogeneity**: forms went from male/female to also transgender and 'do not wish to disclose'.

cards.title: Global impact
lines: World is interconnected: **Apple** is American, manufactures in China, sells worldwide.
A disruption in China or US-China relations hits the whole chain. Gulf or North Korea crises spread similarly.

cards.title: Series of development (slide)
lines: Order: **Europe industrialization -> North America major economic power -> Japan (quality principles) -> China (low-cost manufacturing)**.
Japan: waste removal gives higher quality AND lower cost. China: low-cost base even for American firms.
Europe: mass-produced goods for its **colonies** (India was one). North America: **scale**, belief that good quality costs more.

cards.title: Uncertainty examples
lines: **Kedarnath tragedy** (construction in a vulnerable valley) and **Delhi smog** (causes and cures still debated).
You cannot remove uncertainty, only prepare and mitigate.

cards.title: The way out
lines: Japan = quality benchmark, China = cost benchmark. Matching them is not leadership.
Slide: **What is the way out? Innovation.** A 'bigger line' of new value. Innovation should be **pervasive** across the organisation.

cards.title: Remember 1
lines: **4 pressures**: shrinking PLCs, rising expectations, high uncertainty, global impact.
PLC: introduction, growth, maturity, decline; 10-20 yrs -> 2-3 yrs.
Customers want low cost + high quality + fast delivery together.

cards.title: Remember 2
lines: Japan quality, China cost, **way out = innovation**.
External environment mostly outside a firm's control.

lectures.title: L2 Innovation and Creativity - An Introduction

cards.title: Drucker's definition
lines: Innovation is **the specific tool of entrepreneurs, the means by which they exploit change as an opportunity for a different business or a different service**.
Official **Week 1 Q1**: blank = **Innovation** (not Design, Marketing, Communication).

cards.title: Change -> opportunity (lecturer's examples) (1/2)
lines: Four examples to recognise.

cards.title: The three I's
lines: **Idea, Implementation, Impact.**
Official **Q2**: Idea, Implementation, Impact. Distractors: Integration, Industry.
Idea: keep open, do not judge early. Implementation: execution. Impact: measurable result.

cards.title: Invention vs innovation
lines: **Idea + Implementation = Invention** (lab or experiment stage).
**Invention + Impact = Innovation.** Work left in a file has no impact.
Official **Q3** figure: Invention + Impact = ? -> **Innovation**.

cards.title: Invention defined
lines: New concept executed in a **controlled setting**: lab prototype, project report, dissertation.
Stays in the file, never reaches market = **not innovation**.

cards.title: Idea stage rule
lines: Do **not evaluate** at idea stage: eyes, ears, brain open.
Quantity and novelty first, judgement later. Idea need not be new if implementation is novel.

cards.title: Impact depends on the organisation
lines: Business: market share, cost, profit.
School: students going on to higher education.
Religious organisation: people overcoming addictions.

cards.title: Implementation can be the novelty
lines: **Gandhi's non-violence**: idea was ancient (Jainism, Buddhism). Novelty was implementing it as a mass movement for the freedom struggle.

cards.title: Myths vs realities
lines: Official **Q4**: 'begins with curiosity' TRUE; 'always smooth linear' FALSE.

rows: **Iterative**, outcome of a series of experiments

cards.title: Risk and teamwork
lines: Risk mitigation example: motorbike on a hill (helmet, brakes, speed limit).
Innovation is a **team activity**: one asks, another answers, another tests, another commercialises.

cards.title: Remember 1
lines: Drucker: **specific tool of entrepreneurs**, exploit **change**.
3 I's: **Idea, Implementation, Impact**.
Idea + Implementation = **Invention**; + Impact = **Innovation**.

cards.title: Remember 2
lines: **Curiosity** not creativity; **iterative** not linear; risk + assessment + mitigation.
Team activity.

cards.title: Two challenges
lines: **Resistance to change** and **prediction disability** (slide).

cards.title: Resistance to change: four forms (1/2)
lines: Official **Q5**: **Ignoring the Idea** and **Inertia**. Wrong: 'ignoring the chances of failure', 'ability to exude confidence'.
Lecture form is **fear of failure** (prefer tested formulas).

rows: Idea dismissed (boss ignores junior; parents dismiss career dream)
Failure seen as bad; stick to tested formulas
'I cannot do this'; needs a mentor (Jambavanth reminding Hanuman)

cards.title: VUCA (1/2)
lines: Prediction disability is described by **VUCA**: Volatility, Uncertainty, Complexity, Ambiguity.
Official **Q10**: 'unknown unknowns' = **Ambiguity**.

rows: Unexpected/unstable, maybe unknown duration, not hard to understand; knowledge available (demonetization)
Basic cause and effect known; change possible but not a given
Named; **no definition given** in slides or lecture
Causal links completely unclear; no precedents; **unknown unknowns**

cards.title: Resistance: lecture examples
lines: **Ignoring**: boss dismisses junior; parents dismiss career wish (doctor, engineer, IAS).
**Inertia**: Hanuman needs Jambavanth to remind him of his powers.
Myths are dangerous: believing it is linear leaves founders depressed when profit is not instant.

cards.title: Two systems of thinking
lines: **Emotional/intuitive** and **deliberate/analytical**. Learn to use both (driving: deliberate at first, intuitive with expertise).

cards.title: VUCA: lecture glosses
lines: Volatility: **demonetization**, GST rollout.
Uncertainty: cause-effect known but other factors can shift the outcome.
Ambiguity: no precedent, e.g. new market or product outside core competency. VUCA concept is from **Harvard Business Review**.

cards.title: Elephant and rider
lines: Harmony needed: rider steers elephant off the tiger path to the green-grass path.
No harmony: elephant's inertia takes the old path.

cards.title: Remember 1
lines: Challenges: **resistance to change**, **prediction disability**.
Resistance: ignoring the idea, fear of failure, inertia, lack of confidence. Q5 key: **Ignoring the Idea + Inertia**.

cards.title: Alarm clock
lines: Rider sets the **5 am alarm** at night. Elephant switches it off in the morning.
Progress when emotional side follows the analytical side. Rider handles prediction disability, a mentor/champion handles resistance.

cards.title: Remember 2
lines: VUCA = Volatility, Uncertainty, Complexity, Ambiguity. **Unknown unknowns = Ambiguity**.
Elephant = emotional (heavy, powerful, slow). Rider = analytical (sees, intelligent, powerless).

cards.title: Jugaad vs systematic
lines: **Jugaad**: ad hoc improvised fix (North India), not sustainable.
**Systematic**: planned, in enabling environments (universities, corporations); aims at **IP rights**, commercialisation, technology transfer.

cards.title: Incremental vs breakthrough
lines: Official **Q7**: breakthrough = **steam engine, wheel, fire**. 'Evolution 2G to 3G' is **incremental**, not in the key.
Increments follow breakthroughs; many increments can build a breakthrough. A genuinely new cure is the lecture's hypothetical breakthrough example.

rows: New concept changing the status quo
Fire, wheel, steam engine, landline -> mobile

cards.title: Incremental and breakthrough interact
lines: Breakthrough sets a new level. Incremental work adapts it for real users.
Accumulated increments prepare the next breakthrough.
Incremental happens inside the organisation, so often invisible outside.

cards.title: Frugal innovation
lines: Sees resource constraints **as an opportunity, not a liability**; favours **agility over efficiency**.
Good-quality solutions with **greatest value at lowest cost**; not technically sophisticated to wow customers.
Official **Q6**: both statements TRUE.
Avoid 'marketing myopia'; co-create with customers; often serves underserved people.

cards.title: Four areas of innovation (slide) (1/2)
lines: **Product, Process, Customer Experience, Business Model.**

rows: New/improved goods or services; most visible
Speed post or visa tracking; Facebook birthday/memory reminders
How value is created and captured

cards.title: IPL (touches all four)
lines: Franchise system borrowed from European soccer (business model), 20-20 format (product), new rules (process), entertainment (customer experience).
Categories are not mutually exclusive.

cards.title: Business model innovation
lines: Rethinks how value is **created, delivered and captured**: most encompassing type.
Process innovation (Six Sigma, Lean, TQM, Kanban) is invisible to customers but felt in cost, quality, speed.

cards.title: Remember 1
lines: Jugaad = ad hoc, not sustainable. Systematic = planned, IP.
Incremental = Kaizen, 2G->3G. Breakthrough = fire, wheel, steam engine, landline->mobile.

cards.title: Remember 2
lines: Frugal = constraint as opportunity, agility over efficiency, great value at lowest cost.
4 areas: product, process, customer experience, business model.

cards.title: Can innovation be taught?
lines: Emotions: hard. **Analysis: teachable.**
Teachable (slide): **awareness creation, development of confidence, removal of myths**.
Awareness example: positive campaign ('remove polio from India') vs negative ('take this vaccine to avoid illness').

cards.title: Three schools of creative thinking
lines: **Design thinking, Systems thinking, Lateral thinking.**

rows: Solution-focused, action-oriented, preferred future; human centered; prototyping; rapid iterative improvement; cross-functional teams
Model larger system; **point of leverage**; **silver bullet**; Senge *The Fifth Discipline*; Goldratt **Theory of Constraints** (*The Goal*)
New idea from a known idea in another context; **Six Thinking Hats**

cards.title: Prototyping and 3D printing
lines: Technologies like **3D printing** make prototyping cheap, enabling rapid iteration.

cards.title: Design thinking facts
lines: Official **Q8** (INCORRECT statement): **'product-centered'**. It is solution-focused, action-oriented, **human-centered**.
Human centered = empathy: time with people to see behaviour, emotions, anxieties, aspirations.
Case: demonetization (public feedback, fast rule changes, RBI + banks + police).

cards.title: Systems and lateral thinking examples
lines: Systems: fix one constraint and the next appears (continuous).
Lateral: **IPL** = known franchise idea from European soccer applied to cricket; European solid waste management applied to India.

cards.title: Six Thinking Hats (Edward de Bono) (1/3)
lines: Official **Q9** key: I-C, II-D, III-A, IV-F, V-E, VI-B.
Black hat: barriers, warns of dangers (lecturer calls it the negative person).

cards.title: Demonetization as design thinking
lines: Public feedback, rapid changes: old-note over-the-counter exchange limit **Rs 4,000** then raised, then cut again, then stopped (lecture; exact middle figures not verified).
Coordinated RBI, banks, police, intelligence, government.

cards.title: Remember 1
lines: Teachable: awareness, confidence, removing myths.
Design: human centered, prototyping, rapid iteration, cross-functional. **Not product-centered**.

cards.title: Remember 2
lines: Systems: leverage point, silver bullet, Senge, Goldratt ToC.
Lateral: known idea -> new context; Six Hats (de Bono).

cheatSheet.heading: Week 1 in 10 lines
bullets: Pressures: shrinking PLCs, rising expectations, high uncertainty, global impact -> innovation is the way out.
Drucker: innovation = **specific tool of entrepreneurs** to exploit **change**.
3 I's: **Idea, Implementation, Impact**. Idea + Implementation = Invention; + Impact = Innovation.
Myths: creativity->**curiosity**; linear->**iterative**; risk-taking->risk + assessment + mitigation.
Resistance: **ignoring the idea, fear of failure, inertia, lack of confidence**.
VUCA: Volatility, Uncertainty, Complexity, Ambiguity. **Unknown unknowns = Ambiguity**.
Elephant = emotional, Rider = analytical.
Types: jugaad/systematic; incremental/breakthrough; frugal; product/process/customer experience/business model.
Schools: design, systems, lateral.
Hats: White info, Black barriers, Red feelings, Yellow values/benefits, Green creativity, Blue process.

cheatSheet.heading: Official Week 1 answers (all 10)
bullets: Q1 Innovation
Q2 Idea, Implementation, Impact
Q3 Innovation (Invention + Impact)
Q4 Statement 1 true, Statement 2 false
Q5 Ignoring the Idea; Inertia
Q6 Both true
Q7 Steam engine; wheel; fire
Q8 Design thinking is product-centered (INCORRECT)
Q9 I-C, II-D, III-A, IV-F, V-E, VI-B
Q10 Ambiguity

cheatSheet.heading: Traps
bullets: Q5: 'ignoring the chances of failure' is wrong.
Q7: 2G to 3G is incremental, not breakthrough.
Q8 asks for the INCORRECT statement.
Q10: Ambiguity, not Uncertainty.

cheatSheet.heading: Gaps
bullets: Complexity (VUCA) not defined in lecture or slides.
Company claims (Ola, Alibaba, free apps) are recording-era examples.
